svg.aria-label: The overhead power-line inspection image as a dense-detection primitive. Left: six properties of the frame — tiny defects on large hardware, thin wires that span the frame, a fixed component taxonomy with defect states, cluttered natural backgrounds, a UAV flight plan around a known tower, and extreme class imbalance with few defects. Right: a ladder of six output layers from L0 flight and view planning, L1 image-level normal or defect screening, L2 boxes per component, L3 masks of wires, towers and corridor hazards, L4 component state such as missing pin or broken shell, to L5 maintenance ticket and risk per span.
svg.title: The power-line inspection image: six properties, six output layers
svg.text: The power-line inspection image: six frame properties, six output layers
UAV, helicopter or robot patrol of transmission towers and spans. The utility needs a repair ticket per tower, not a box.

g.text: A missing split pin is ~10 px in a 6000 px frame.
Boxes fail; lines need masks, curves or keypoints.
Insulator, damper, clamp, bolt, pin × missing/broken/rusted.
Forest, fields, roads, sky glare and the tower lattice itself.
5 · A planned viewpoint around a known asset
The UAV orbits the tower; framing is a control choice.
Defects are rare; most utility datasets are never released.
L5 · Repair ticket, risk per span
missing pin, broken shell, flashover, corrosion (§4, §6)
L3 · Masks: wires, towers, corridor hazards
L2 · Boxes per component and defect

svg.text: Colours: grey = capture and screening, green = geometry, orange = decisions. Section numbers refer to the 2026-Oct-13 report.
